items.q: Third one on the right, that’s my home. Chuck Connors in front of me, Russell Procope to the right.

ctx.x: I was going mouth him. So Mercer was managing the band at the time, called Jimmy and said, “We need a trombone player for two Sundays.” And Jimmy recommended me. I got the call for that gig. I remember being, right around then I was out at my mom’s house with someone else and I just pulled out a record I said, “This is who I’m playing with next week.” I was like — and I remember calling people and the big advice I got, not from Jimmy, from someone else said, “Make sure you don’t sit in someone’s seat on the bus.”…

to talk business here, but call me tomorrow or something.” I was like, some friends of mine who lived in Boston, I was staying with them, I was like whoa, I was like blown away. Then I talked to him a day or two later and so I’m on the phone and he says, “Well how much do you want?” Oh, no, actually, we didn’t even talk money. He just said, “Well we’re leaving ten days from now, and then in a month we’re going to Europe, we’re going to Africa for about five or six weeks.” I was like ohh, this is amazing. Then…
